label: Does it split into clear, separate business areas?
help: E.g. orders, payments and inventory that change for different reasons.

label: It mainly reacts to events or runs background work
help: E.g. sensor readings, notifications, order-placed events.

label: Very high or sharply spiky concurrent load
help: E.g. ticket drops or flash sales where thousands arrive at once.

label: It processes data in sequential steps
help: E.g. ETL, media conversion, batch jobs.

label: Needs plug-ins, extensions or per-customer customisation
help: E.g. an IDE with extensions, or rules that differ per client.

label: Workflows must be strictly controlled and predictable
help: E.g. every loan application goes through the same steps in order.

label: Constant, heavy, predictable load around the clock
help: E.g. a busy API that never sleeps.

label: Failures must only affect a subset of customers
help: Large multi-tenant platforms where one outage must not hit everyone.

label: Users or devices share directly with each other
help: Little or no central server, e.g. file sharing or local-first apps.

label: Must process near devices or keep working offline on site
help: Ultra-low latency or unreliable networks, e.g. factory floors.

label: Most expected changes are technical
help: E.g. swapping the UI framework or database, rather than new business features.

label: Parts of the system have very different needs
help: E.g. a public site with huge traffic and a small back office.

label: Several teams will work on one large web frontend
help: Each team owns part of the same website.

label: Where will it run?
help: Some styles need a cloud provider.

label: Must avoid vendor lock-in
help: You must be able to move to another provider.

label: Strict all-or-nothing transactions across the whole system
help: E.g. money must never be half-transferred.

label: Migrating from an existing monolith
help: You're replacing or splitting an old system.

label: Regulated data (health, finance, personal data)
help: Laws or auditors set rules for the data.
